title: Bounded finite-evaluation replacement of a cocycle by a rectangle residual
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, a profinite group $G$, an open subgroup $H\subseteq G$ of index $m$ prime to $\ell$, an integer $n\geq1$, and $a_0,\ldots,a_n\in G$. For a nonarchimedean normed $\mathbf Q_\ell$-vector space $V$ (not necessarily complete), with $\|v\|=0$ exactly for $v=0$, $\|a v\|=|a|_\ell\|v\|$ and $\|v+w\|\leq\max(\|v\|,\|w\|)$, and with the norm topology, set $C^r(G,V)=C(G^r,V)$, with trivial group action and differential
$$(dc)(g_1,\ldots,g_{r+1})=c(g_2,\ldots,g_{r+1})+\sum_{i=1}^r(-1)^i c(g_1,\ldots,g_ig_{i+1},\ldots,g_{r+1})+(-1)^{r+1}c(g_1,\ldots,g_r),$$
where $d^0=0$. There are linear operators $T:C^n(G,V)\to C^{n-1}(G,V)$ and $R:C^n(G,V)\to C^n(G,V)$ given by fixed finite sums of evaluations
$$(Tc)(x)=\sum_{j=1}^u\alpha_j c(\psi_j(x)),\qquad (Rc)(y)=\sum_{j=1}^v\beta_j c(\chi_j(y)),$$
where $\psi_j:G^{n-1}\to G^n$ and $\chi_j:G^n\to G^n$ are continuous, $\alpha_j,\beta_j\in\mathbf Q_\ell$ have absolute value at most one, and all these choices depend only on $G,H,n,(a_i)$, not on $V$. For every cocycle $c$, $Rc$ is a cocycle and $c=d(Tc)+Rc$. If the homogeneous function $f_c(g_0,\ldots,g_n)=c(g_0^{-1}g_1,\ldots,g_{n-1}^{-1}g_n)$ vanishes on $Ha_0\times\cdots\times Ha_n$, then $Rc=0$. The operators have supremum-norm bound one, preserve every $\mathbf Q_\ell$-linear coefficient subspace, and apply to continuous profinite parameter families by leaving the parameter fixed; the resulting families are continuous. The conventions for $\mathbf Q_\ell$ and universes are [def-weil-l-adic-numbers], [def-weil-size-convention].

proof.text: Use [lem-sfb-topological-homogeneous-cochain-coordinates] for $E=\mathbf Q_\ell$, $J=G$ and the trivial action. The norm axioms give continuous addition and scalar multiplication on $V$, so its topological-vector-space hypotheses hold without completeness. Write $\Psi c=f_c$ and $\Phi F(g_1,\ldots,g_q)=F(1,g_1,g_1g_2,\ldots,g_1\cdots g_q)$. The cited statement gives inverse linear cochain maps, including degree zero, and $\delta\Psi=\Psi d$, $\Phi\delta=d\Phi$. In particular $c$ is a cocycle exactly when $F=\Psi c$ satisfies $\delta F=0$. We will construct finite-evaluation operators on the diagonally $G$-invariant homogeneous functions and then conjugate them by these explicit maps.

proof.text: Choose a transversal $D\subset G$ for the finitely many right cosets $H\backslash G$, including $1$. Write $x=\rho(x)s(x)$ uniquely with $\rho(x)\in H$ and $s(x)\in D$. Each coset $Hs$ is clopen: it is open by translation, and its complement is a union of other open cosets. On $Hs$, $\rho(x)=xs^{-1}$ is continuous into $H$ with its subspace topology; these open pieces show that $\rho:G\to H$ is continuous. Uniqueness gives $\rho(hx)=h\rho(x)$ for $h\in H$. The transversal is fixed once, independently of $V$. No normality of $H$ is assumed.

proof.text: For a set $Y$ let $B_q(Y)$ be the free abelian group with specified basis $[y_0,\ldots,y_q]$ (repetitions allowed), and put $B_{-1}(Y)=\mathbf Z[\varnothing]$. This is the basis convention of [def-weil-pbc-free-module]. Define $\partial$ by alternating deletion, including $\partial[y]=[\varnothing]$ and $\partial[\varnothing]=0$. Deleting two distinct positions in opposite orders gives opposite signs, hence $\partial^2=0$. A homogeneous function $F$ extends uniquely by finite sums to $\widehat F:B_n(G)\to V$; then $\delta F=0$ means $\widehat F\partial=0$ on $B_{n+1}(G)$. Left translation acts coordinatewise on all these chains.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-ordered-join-partial-contraction] with $r=n+1$ and the separately labelled sets $X_i=Ha_i$. Write $J_q$ for its ordered-color chains and $e_q:J_q\to B_q(G)$ for erasing colors; $\partial e=e\partial$ follows from deletion. For $h\in H$, choose anchors $v_i=ha_i$ and denote the cited operator by $S^h$. Its statement gives $\partial S^h_q+S^h_{q-1}\partial=1$ for $-1\leq q\leq n-1$, its naturality under simultaneous left translation, and a fixed finite integer expansion using only vertex insertions and replacements. In degree $n$, every basis of $J_n$ has exactly one vertex in each color, in order $0,\ldots,n$; thus every tuple in $e_n(J_n)$ is an integer combination of tuples in the specified rectangle.

proof.text:
Construct $P_q:B_q(G)\to J_q$ through degree $n$. Put $P_{-1}=1$ and $P_0[x]=[(0,\rho(x)a_0)]$, so $\partial P_0=P_{-1}\partial$. For $1\leq q\leq n$, assuming the chain identities below degree $q$, define on each basis tuple $x=[x_0,\ldots,x_q]$
$$z=P_{q-1}(\partial x),\qquad P_q(x)=S^{\rho(x_0)}_{q-1}(z),$$
and extend linearly. The induction hypothesis gives $\partial z=P_{q-2}\partial^2x=0$, using the augmentation identity when $q=1$. Since $q-1\leq n-1$, [lem-sfb-ordered-join-partial-contraction] gives $\partial P_q(x)=z$. Hence $\partial P_q=P_{q-1}\partial$ in all required degrees. The input-dependent anchor is chosen on basis tuples before linear extension; it is not asserted to be a linear function of a general chain.

proof.text: Naturality in [lem-sfb-ordered-join-partial-contraction], applied to left translation by $h\in H$, gives $hS^{\rho(x_0)}z=S^{h\rho(x_0)}(hz)$. Together with $\rho(hx_0)=h\rho(x_0)$ this proves inductively $P_q(hx)=hP_q(x)$; the base case is the displayed $P_0$. The finite-expansion clause of that node also proves inductively that $P_q[x_0,\ldots,x_q]$ is a fixed finite integer sum of colored tuples with vertices of the form $\rho(x_j)a_i$. Boundary merely selects subtuples, and the next $S$ inserts or replaces by $\rho(x_0)a_i$. Coefficient lists and coordinate selections depend on the degree and color lists alone. Keep repeated terms rather than combining them, so no equality test on input values enters this expansion.

proof.text:
Set $A_q=e_qP_q$ for $-1\leq q\leq n$. These are $H$-equivariant augmented chain maps and $A_{-1}=1$. For $b\in G$, let $C_b$ prefix $b$ to a tuple, with $C_b[\varnothing]=[b]$. Direct deletion gives
$$\partial[b,y_0,\ldots,y_q]=[y_0,\ldots,y_q]-C_b\partial[y_0,\ldots,y_q],$$
so $\partial C_b+C_b\partial=1$, also in degree $-1$ since $\partial[b]=[\varnothing]$. Coordinatewise translation gives $hC_bz=C_{hb}(hz)$.

proof.text:
Define $Q_{-1}=0$ and, on basis tuples $x=[x_0,\ldots,x_q]$, recursively for $0\leq q\leq n$ put
$$Z_q(x)=x-A_qx-Q_{q-1}\partial x,\qquad Q_q(x)=C_{x_0}Z_q(x),$$
extending linearly. The augmentation of $Z_0$ is $1-1=0$. For $q\geq1$, the previous-degree identity and the chain identity for $A$ give
$$\partial Z_q=(1-A_{q-1})\partial x-(1-A_{q-1}-Q_{q-2}\partial)\partial x=0.$$
The prefix identity therefore gives $\partial Q_q(x)=Z_q(x)$. This proves by induction
$$1-A_q=\partial Q_q+Q_{q-1}\partial\qquad(0\leq q\leq n).$$
Both the base and the step have been verified, rather than invoking an unspecified resolution-comparison theorem.

proof.text: Induction in this same recursion proves $H$-equivariance of $Q$: $Z_q(hx)=hZ_q(x)$ and $C_{hx_0}(hZ_q(x))=hQ_q(x)$. Its base is $Q_{-1}=0$. Likewise the finite expansion for $A$, together with deletion, subtraction and prefixing, proves that each $Q_q[x_0,\ldots,x_q]$ has a fixed finite integer expansion with every vertex either $x_j$ or $\rho(x_j)a_i$. These vertex maps are continuous by step 2 and multiplication in $G$. Thus evaluation of any continuous $F$ on $Q_q$ or $A_q$ is continuous. All the recursions are integral and independent of coefficients.

proof.text:
For any degree-$n$ homogeneous $G$-invariant function $F$, define $H$-invariant functions
$$UF(x_0,\ldots,x_{n-1})=\widehat F(Q_{n-1}[x_0,\ldots,x_{n-1}]),\quad WF(y_0,\ldots,y_n)=\widehat F(A_n[y_0,\ldots,y_n]).$$
They are linear in $F$ and continuous by step 9. If $\delta F=0$, applying $\widehat F$ to step 8 in degree $n$ gives $F=\delta(UF)+WF$, because $\widehat F\partial Q_n=0$. Applying $\delta$ gives $\delta(WF)=0$, since $\delta^2=0$ by the same deletion cancellation as for $\partial^2$. If $F$ vanishes on $Ha_0\times\cdots\times Ha_n$, then $WF=0$ by the degree-$n$ description of $eJ_n$ in step 4. These are identities on $G$-tuples, before passing to cohomology.

proof.text:
For an $H$-invariant degree-$q$ homogeneous function $L$ on $G^{q+1}$ define
$$(\mathcal M_qL)(x)=m^{-1}\sum_{s\in D}L(sx_0,\ldots,sx_q).$$
For $g\in G$, write $sg=h u$ with $h\in H$ and $u\in D$. Right multiplication permutes $H\backslash G$, so $s\mapsto u$ is a permutation, and $L(sgx)=L(hux)=L(ux)$. Thus $\mathcal M_qL$ is $G$-invariant, without normality of $H$. Deletion commutes with each simultaneous translation, so $\delta\mathcal M=\mathcal M\delta$. On $G$-invariant functions $\mathcal M F=F$. Therefore for cocycles step 10 gives
$$F=\delta(\mathcal M_{n-1}UF)+\mathcal M_nWF,\qquad\delta(\mathcal M_nWF)=0.$$
The residual is zero whenever $F$ vanishes on the rectangle. The finite sum also preserves continuity and linearity.

proof.text:
Define on all of $C^n(G,V)$
$$T=\Phi_{n-1}\mathcal M_{n-1}U\Psi_n,\qquad R=\Phi_n\mathcal M_nW\Psi_n.$$
The cochain identities of [lem-sfb-topological-homogeneous-cochain-coordinates] and step 11 give $c=d(Tc)+Rc$ and $d(Rc)=0$ for every cocycle. Its inverse formula is exactly $\Psi_nc=f_c$ for the trivial action, so rectangle vanishing gives $Rc=0$. To obtain the finite evaluation formulas on the full cochain spaces, expand $Q_{n-1},A_n$ as in steps 6 and 9, translate each tuple by each $s\in D$, insert the cumulative-product tuple from $\Phi$, and replace each final homogeneous tuple $(b_0,\ldots,b_n)$ by $(b_0^{-1}b_1,\ldots,b_{n-1}^{-1}b_n)$ from $\Psi$. These are continuous maps of exactly the domains and codomains in the item, also when $n-1=0$. All coefficients are integers divided by $m$, and every choice was independent of $V$.

proof.text: Every integer $k$ has $|k|_\ell\leq1$, while $|m|_\ell=1$ because $m$ is prime to $\ell$, by [def-weil-l-adic-numbers]. Hence every coefficient $k/m$ in the expansions has absolute value at most one. The ultrametric inequality now gives pointwise $\|(Tc)(x)\|\leq\sup_z\|c(z)\|$ and $\|(Rc)(y)\|\leq\sup_z\|c(z)\|$. These suprema are finite: the continuous real function $\|c(-)\|$ has compact image on the compact domain $G^n$. Taking suprema proves both operator bounds. Each value of each operator is a finite $\mathbf Q_\ell$-linear combination of values of $c$, so every linear coefficient subspace is preserved, whether or not it is closed. In particular the formulas never require a limit in $V$.

proof.text: Let $S$ be any profinite parameter space and $c:S\times G^n\to V$ continuous. Apply the same fixed formulas to the group variables only: for example $(Tc)(s,x)=\sum_j\alpha_j c(s,\psi_j(x))$. Each map $(s,x)\mapsto(s,\psi_j(x))$ is continuous, and finite addition and fixed scalar multiplication are continuous in $V$. This proves continuity of the resulting families, and the cochain and rectangle identities hold separately at every parameter. If $S$ is empty there is the unique family. For $n=1$, $Q_0[x]=[x,x]-[x,\rho(x)a_0]$ and the degree-$1$ homotopy identity still applies; after averaging $UF$ is a $G$-invariant function of one variable and hence constant, so its inhomogeneous differential is the stipulated $d^0=0$. Thus the bottom degree and incomplete or zero coefficient spaces are included.
